questions.question: What does relative dating determine?
choices: The exact numerical age of every rock
The time taken to erode an entire landscape
Whether an event is older or younger than another
The temperature at which a fossil formed

questions.question: In an undisturbed sequence of sedimentary layers, where are the oldest layers normally found?
choices: At the top
At the bottom
Only in the middle
Only on the western side

questions.question: What is a trace fossil?
choices: A mineral replacement of an organism's body tissue
A modern organism collected for comparison
A fossil shell preserved as an original body part
Preserved evidence of an organism's activity

questions.question: What is an unconformity in a rock sequence?
choices: A layer showing continuous deposition without a gap
A boundary between minerals within one crystal
A surface that always has younger rocks below older rocks
A surface representing missing geologic time

questions.question: What makes an index fossil useful for correlating rock layers?
choices: Occurrence at only one site over all of Earth's history
Wide distribution and a relatively short geologic time range
A large body size regardless of age
An absence from sedimentary rocks

questions.question: What process underlies radiometric dating?
choices: A constant rate of sediment deposition in every setting
The gradual darkening of rock with age
Predictable radioactive decay of isotopes
The rate at which every fossil increases in size

questions.question: Which geologic era includes most of the time non-avian dinosaurs lived?
choices: Mesozoic
Cenozoic
Paleozoic
Archean

questions.question: Why is the fossil record incomplete?
choices: All organisms leave equally complete fossils
Preservation requires conditions that do not occur for every organism
Only modern organisms can be fossilized
Sedimentary rocks never preserve biological remains

questions.question: Why are hard body parts often preserved more readily than soft tissues?
choices: They resist decay and destruction better under many conditions
Soft tissues cannot ever be preserved
Hard parts always fossilize without burial
Soft tissues decay only in modern organisms

questions.question: How can a volcanic ash layer help estimate the age of fossils in nearby layers?
choices: Ash automatically gives every nearby fossil the same exact age
Ash minerals date the living organism directly without context
Suitable ash minerals can be radiometrically dated
Ash thickness alone gives an exact age

questions.question: Why is carbon-14 dating unsuitable for dinosaur fossils tens of millions of years old?
choices: Carbon-14 dating works only for inorganic crystals
Carbon-14 has too long a half-life for ancient material
The organism's size determines the isotope's half-life
Too little original carbon-14 remains after so much time

questions.question: What do marine fossils in rocks far inland suggest about the rock's environment of formation?
choices: The area has always had its present climate and elevation
The area was once covered by water supporting marine life
Marine fossils cannot be preserved outside today's oceans
All marine fossils were transported by modern rivers

questions.question: Why does a fault cutting through several rock layers indicate the fault is younger than those layers?
choices: Faults form before any rock exists
Older layers cannot be broken
The fault's color determines its age
The layers had to exist before they could be cut

questions.question: How does an intrusion's age compare with the rock it cuts?
choices: The intrusion is younger
The intrusion is always older
Both must have identical ages
Their ages depend only on their thickness

questions.question: Why are fossils and radiometric dates used together?
choices: Fossils alone provide exact calendar years
Radiometric methods directly date every fossil equally well
They provide complementary evidence for correlating and dating events
Both methods provide only the rock's mineral composition

questions.question: Layer A lies below B, and B below C, with no disturbance. Which order is oldest to youngest?
choices: C, B, A
B, A, C
A, B, C
A, C, B

questions.question: A fossil-bearing layer lies between ash layers dated 12 and 10 million years old. What age range is consistent with the fossil layer?
choices: Between 10 and 12 million years
Between 1 and 2 million years
Older than 20 million years
Younger than 1 million years

questions.question: Half of a radioactive parent isotope remains after one half-life. How much remains after two half-lives?
choices: One-half
Three-fourths
None
One-fourth

questions.question: Two distant rock layers contain the same suitable index fossil. What does this support?
choices: They must have identical thickness
They formed during a similar geologic time interval
They formed in the same exact location
They contain equal amounts of every mineral

questions.question: An erosion surface separates two sedimentary units. What should a geologist consider?
choices: Some time may be missing from the local rock record
Deposition was necessarily continuous
The upper unit must be older
The surface proves no organisms existed then
